overview: Singapore is a city-state on the southern tip of the Malay Peninsula. It became independent in 1965, after two years as part of Malaysia, and in a few decades grew into one of the world's richest countries and busiest ports. English, Malay, Mandarin and Tamil are all official languages.

geography.text: Singapore is made up of one main island and around 60 smaller ones, separated from Malaysia by the narrow Johor Strait. It is low-lying, and land reclaimed from the sea has made the country about a quarter bigger since the 1960s. Although it is one of the most densely populated countries, it calls itself a 'city in a garden', with many parks and nature reserves.

history.text: Singapore was a small fishing and trading settlement when Stamford Raffles set up a British trading post there in 1819, and it grew into a major port. Japan occupied it during the Second World War. Singapore joined Malaysia in 1963, became independent in 1965 and, under Lee Kuan Yew, grew into one of the world's richest countries.

events.title: British trading post
events.text: Stamford Raffles founds a British settlement.

government.text: Singapore is a parliamentary republic. The People's Action Party has won every general election since independence in 1965. The Prime Minister leads the government, and the President, elected directly, is head of state. The government is known for being efficient but also for strict laws.

economy.text: Singapore is one of the richest countries in the world and a global centre for finance, shipping and trade. Its port is one of the busiest on Earth. It also makes computer chips, medicines and chemicals.

culture.text: Singapore is a mix of Chinese, Malay, Indian and other cultures, and its four official languages are English, Malay, Mandarin and Tamil. Hawker centres, food courts with cheap stalls, are listed by UNESCO. Gardens by the Bay has giant 'supertrees'.

items.title: Hawker centres
items.text: Open-air food courts, listed by UNESCO in 2020.

sport.text: Singapore hosted the first night race in Formula 1 in 2008. Swimmer Joseph Schooling won Singapore's first Olympic gold in 2016, beating his hero Michael Phelps.

items.text: Joseph Schooling won Olympic 100 m butterfly gold.
